children: To address privacy concerns and a class action lawsuit in California, Meta Platforms
is expected to unveil smart glasses without a camera at Wednesday’s Connect conference.

According to Reuters, camera-free smart glasses will come in two styles, Clubmaster and Burbank, along with a new version of its Meta Ray-Ban glasses with a camera and a thinner and lighter pair of augmented-reality glasses codenamed Phoenix.

The glasses are currently equipped with a built-in, high-resolution digital camera to capture point-of-view photos and videos that can be activated either through a physical button in the temple of the glasses or by using a voice command. Once deployed, a white LED light activates on the front of the glasses to notify people the camera is active.
But despite the LED recording light, the ability to capture or film unsuspecting subjects has now drawn criticisms from privacy advocates and has even been restricted in several UK public spaces.

also face a federal class-action lawsuit in California over alleged privacy violations involving their smart glasses. The suit claims consumers were misled about the devices’ privacy protections and that the glasses covertly captured and transmitted private and intimate footage to offshore human contractors for AI training, with cameras often activated without users’ knowledge.
Connect 2026 is being held on Wednesday and Thursday with a keynote address from CEO Mark Zuckerberg at 4pm PT (7pm ET).

title: Meta expected to address privacy concerns with camera-free smart glasses
